JPM.rationale: JPMorgan Chase demonstrates strong fundamental health and positive trajectory. Q1 2026 showed record net income of $16.49B with EPS of $5.94, representing 10% YoY revenue growth and 17.2% EPS growth. The bank maintains industry-leading ROE of 16.2% and net margins of 31.5%, with a diversified business model across Consumer & Community Banking, Commercial & Investment Bank, and Asset & Wealth Management. The bank passed the 2026 stress test with a strong 14.3% tier 1 capital ratio and announced a $50B buyback plus 10% dividend increase, signaling management confidence. Valuation is reasonable at 15.5x P/E, sitting in the middle of its 13.7-17.8x range over the past year, and P/B of 2.5x is also mid-range. The near-term catalyst is the Q2 2026 earnings report on July 14, with consensus expecting EPS of $5.49-5.52 on revenue of $48.71B. However, the stock has closed lower after each of its last four earnings reports, and the stock is trading near all-time highs at $335.47, which limits the upside from current levels. Macro headwinds include rising 10-year Treasury yields (4.54%) and a flattening yield curve (T10Y2Y at 0.38%), which could pressure net interest margins. The score reflects solid fundamentals and a reasonable valuation, tempered by the stock's proximity to record highs and the pattern of post-earnings weakness.
